revised: v2 renames and splits categories to match the reporting taxonomy: direct_change, negation, mention_vs_request, tokenless_implicit, cross_message, quoted_forwarded, contradiction, ambiguity, prompt_injection, social_engineering, obfuscation, benign_preregistered, benign_low_risk_field.
note: Capability categories assigned AFTER both case sets were frozen and after the first evaluation run. This file annotates cases; it does not relabel them and does not change any expected_decision. It lives outside frozen_v1.json and frozen_v2.json so both frozen sets stay byte-for-byte untouched.
why: Aggregate accuracy hides where a system actually differs from another: a rules engine and a model can score similarly overall while failing on completely different categories. The categories below separate what needs reading from what needs matching from what needs normalising.

categories.direct_change: An unambiguous request to change a payment destination or payment instruction, in the live part of the message. Matching handles these; the model adds nothing and this category is the sanity floor.
categories.negation: The email denies, withdraws or warns against a change, usually using the same vocabulary as a real request. Requires reading 'not' in context.
categories.mention_vs_request: Payment details are mentioned, quoted, confirmed or asked about, but nothing is requested. Requires distinguishing talking about a destination from asking for it to change.
categories.tokenless_implicit: A change is asserted but the destination values are not present in the message body - they are in an attachment, an image, or nowhere. Requires reporting that nothing could be verified, rather than reporting nothing.
categories.cross_message: The change has to be reconstructed across a reply chain, where older and newer details both appear and only one is live. Requires tracking which end of the thread is authoritative.
categories.quoted_forwarded: The payload arrives inside forwarded or quoted content - a forwarded attack, a quoted historical detail. Requires attributing content to the right sender.
categories.contradiction: The email contradicts itself or the record: two candidate destinations, a branch code that does not match the bank, mutually inconsistent values. Requires noticing the conflict rather than picking a value.
categories.ambiguity: A change is present but disguised or underspecified - a near-miss number sold as a correction, a value that could be a typo or a substitution. Requires judgement about whether the difference is the point.
categories.prompt_injection: Instructions aimed at the automated reader, hidden in the body, the subject, a quote, white text or a signature block.
categories.social_engineering: Pressure or false authority aimed at the control or the process: urgency, claimed pre-approval, a reference number, staged unavailability.
categories.obfuscation: Character-level evasion: zero-width spaces, soft hyphens, non-breaking hyphens, fullwidth digits, Cyrillic look-alikes. Deterministic to defeat once normalised, invisible until then.
categories.benign_preregistered: A change to a destination already on file as a pre-registered alternate. Should CLEAR; holding it is pure review cost.
categories.benign_low_risk_field: A change to a field that is not a payment destination: contact details, an advice mailbox on a verified domain, commercial terms.
